Amazon WoW Interview Experience
For 2022 Summer Internship
Gauri Shewale
T.Y.BTech CE 2019-2023
gvshewale_b19@ce.vjti.ac.in
What is Amazon Wow?
Amazon WoW is a networking platform for all women engineering students in India that
connects them to Amazon leaders, recruiters, and the broader Amazon community. The platform
provides an opportunity to participate in skill building sessions, utilize available resources,
converse with alumni on their career experiences, and be acquainted with the culture at Amazon.
The objective is to help women students build long-term careers in technology.
So,
I had applied for the 2 months SDE intern role through Amazon WOW drive 2021. There
were a total of 3 online rounds for people who applied for a 2 months internship program and 4-5
rounds for people applying for a 6 months internship program.
Round 1
(17th August,2021)    (1hr 30mins)
It was an online test on Mettl Platform, consisting of 9 sections :
1 Hands on Programming Section :
(Coding Question was not same for all)
And rest (40-45 MCQs total) section wise (4-5 in each) :
●
Data Structures
●
Algorithms
●
Linux
●
Pseudo Coding
●
Networking
●
Software Testing (2 sections)
●
SQL queries
There was no negative marking for the multiple-choice questions.

Hands on Programming Question:
A company has hired N interns, label from 1 to N. Each intern is given a device which
generates a number everyday that will be used as a password for their authentication at the
office door every day in the morning. The internship is for 50 days numbered from 0 to 49.
Initially, (on the 1st day) the number in the device of kth intern will be equal to (5000^k).
From the 2nd day (i.e i=1), a new number will be generated every day in each device in the
following way:
Day(i) = Day(i-1) + 5000 + i
Find the label of an intern from the given password used by him/her.
Input Specification:
Input1 : N, number of interns
Input2 : P, password used
Output Specification:
Return the label of the intern to whom the given password belongs to.
Examples
1)
Input:  N = 15, P = 15000
Output: 3   // Day 0
2)
Input:  N = 25, P = 25003
Output: 3   // Day 2
I was able to solve the coding question with all test cases passed and did almost all the MCQs.
Got the selection for Round 2  mail on Aug 20, 2021 ( i.e on 3rd day after Round 1 )
Round 2
(25th August,2021)    (2hr 25mins)
It was an online test conducted on the AMCAT platform.
It consisted of 4 sections:  (No Switching allowed between on-going sections)
●
Debugging section :
(20 mins)
It consisted of 7 very easy code snippets which had to be debugged to get the desired
output.

●
Coding section :
(2 questions)
(70 mins)    (Coding Questions were not same for all)
Q.1 Given an array of integers, and a value m, return the number of distinct elements
(should be minimum) after removing m elements from array
Example:
Arr= [1,2,2,4,4,3] , m=2
Output: 2
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/minimum-number-of-distinct-elements-after-removing-m-it
ems/
Q.2 Engineers at Amazon are interested in knowing which software component moves
the fastest by counting the number of lines of codes changed in that component and all
the subcomponents in the code base over a month. Component nodes have
subcomponent nodes that make up the larger component.
We’ve stored the components as a tree where each node represents one component that
contains the number of lines changed that month. Software component speed is
computed as the average number of lines of code changed for a given component and all
its subcomponents. Engineers compute this software component speed for all such
components which have one or more subcomponents. Find the component with the
highest software component speed. Assume there will be at least one subcomponent in
the tree and that there will be no ties.
Input:
rootComponent    ------> which is a node representing the root Component node.
Output:
Return a ComponentNode that has the highest software component speed.
Example:
Input:
rootComponent:
200
/       \
120         180
/  |  \         /   \
110 20 30  150 80
Output :  180  node

Explanation:
120 = (120+110+20+30)/4 =70
180 = (180+150+80)/3 =136.667
200 = (200+120+180+110+20+30+150+80)/7= 111.25
https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/349617 (This will be helpful)
●
Workstyle Assessment (20 mins)
It was a nice BIG survey wherein Amazon principles should be kept in mind.
●
Logical Reasoning Section (35mins)   25 questions
Normal ABC: BDF :: EGH ? Type of Questions ..  There were some English
comprehension questions too..
I did the debugging and the Logical Reasoning section completely and was able to do the first
coding problem with all the test cases passed and the second problem with some test cases
passed. ( Late click hua missing corner case in my code for 2nd problem ;) )
After 15 days, I got an email that I have been shortlisted for the interview round.
Round 3
(Interview)    (18th September,2021)    (1hr)
Interview was on Amazon Chime and a live code pair link was provided.
The interviewer introduced himself and asked me directly to speak about one of my
projects. I explained to him briefly using the STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) method and my
contribution in the same. Then he gave me two DSA questions to solve.
1) Given an input array of building heights,return an Output array wherein
Output_arr[i] = Number of buildings visible on left side from the top of Input_arr[i]
Input    100 80 60 70 60 75 85
Output  0     1    1    2    1    4   6
Try this one https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/the-stock-span-problem/
2) He then gave me a code of linked list , and asked some questions regarding the same.
Then
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sum-of-two-linked-lists/
Both variations ( numbers stored in reverse and proper order )
I explained my brute force approach and optimised approach for each with time + space
complexities. Then after getting approval, I wrote the code for the optimised approaches and did
dry runs. My interviewer was a very nice person and patiently listened to my answer discussion.

At the end, he asked me if I had any questions for him, for which I asked him regarding projects
that interns get to work on, his experience with the company, etc. (ALWAYS ASK QUESTION, it
shows that you have interest in the company)
PS: I had one more interviewer in the interview round but he didn’t ask me a single question :)
So be prepared mentally also, to face more than one interviewer.
I was totally not expecting this but luckily got the selection mail 5 days later :D

TIPS:
●
Firstly, do not dive directly into the coding. Do this for each problem
SOLVE THE PROBLEM
(THINK HOW Input -> Output. Keep corner cases also in mind)
OPTIMIZE THE SOLUTION
(How you can reduce Time Complexity, Space Complexity..)
WRITE THE CODE
(Once approach is clear then coding becomes simple)
TEST THE CODE by DRY RUN
(Check how code works on test case manually)
DEBUG THE CODE if errors found
(Errors will come but fear not... check the code line by line)
NOTE- TIME & SPACE COMPLEXITY
(Make a habit of this)
●
In interviews,  start with a brute force approach and then proceed to the optimal solution
even if you know the optimal solution perfectly.  This helps you in getting the hang of the
problem and the interviewer gets to know that you did try to understand the process of
reaching your final solution. There will be follow-up questions based on your answer (like
on data structures used..etc) so be prepared.

●
DO NOT EVER LIE ON YOUR RESUME. The interviewers have seen hundreds of students
before you and you will get caught because they will grill you on that. Be thorough with
your resume.
●
REMEMBER THAT THE INTERVIEWER IS NOT YOUR ENEMY.  Ask for clarifications
regarding problems. They do give you a lot of hints to solve the problems.
●
THINK OUT LOUD.  The interviewers are not mind readers... so talk. Tell them honestly
even if you are not sure about your solution. IT IS OKAY if you don’t know everything or
you are not able to solve the problem completely. Your approach and way of thinking is
judged mostly. (Silence here won’t help you)
●
Always have a look at some interview experiences beforehand. Checkout Geeks For
Geeks and COC drive. Very Helpful.
●
PRACTICE YOUR TECHNICAL INTRODUCTION. Seems like a very obvious thing but at
that moment when you are nervous and remember social awkwardness, you tend to miss
out things about yourself. Practice in front of a mirror if you are bad at speaking English.
●
Each interview teaches you something you need to work on. (I gave 4 interviews before
Amazon. So I learnt a lot from each. ) Some Rounds will go well, others will be like “Nope
..That was bad”. Be Ready anyway. Stay alert and active on Whatsapp and emails. There
have been cases wherein you get called within 15 mins right after the previous round.
●
DON’T FORGET TO RESEARCH ABOUT THE COMPANY. The interviewer will probably ask
you about the company’s mission, vision, principles or what it does. (HR rounds
guaranteed)
●
Prepare for behavioral questions too. We generally study technical questions and
completely ignore behavioral questions.
●
ALWAYS ASK the interviewer something when they ask you whether you have any
questions for them. Be prepared with some questions beforehand. It shows that you do
have interest in the company.
●
Stay Calm and focused during the interviews and the entire process. Things don’t always
go the way you wished them to. Don’t lose hope. Don’t Give up. EVER. There’s always a
next company, next opportunity.
All the best!  You can do it! (✿^‿^ )
